evals.prompt:
The issue is in review. The diff adds a review-thread step: it reads threads with pr.review-comments, checks each against the diff, fixes only a comment that holds, replies with pr.review-reply from review-reply-template.md, and leaves the thread open. The step does not say what happens when the list is empty. Two review threads are open on that diff.

Thread A: "When the list is empty the step should say there were no review comments and stop."

Thread B: "Resolve each thread after the reply."

The reply operation has no resolve flag. Resolving a thread is out of scope.
evals.expected_output: Thread A holds, so the step gains an empty-list stop and that fix is pushed. Thread B does not hold, so it changes no code. Both threads get one reply from the template, in the comment's language, with no work-item id and no tool name, and both stay open.
assertions: The agent reads the threads with pr.review-comments
The agent checks each thread against the diff before changing code
Thread A is fixed in the code because the comment holds
Thread B changes no code
Each thread gets one pr.review-reply taken from review-reply-template.md
Neither reply names a work item, a tracker, an assistant or a plugin
Neither reply starts with a status marker
Neither thread is resolved

evals.prompt: Merge and close NER-620. Its PR is green and approved, and the user's guide for it is already in nerdbrain. NER-620 has a sub-issue NER-621, which is still in Todo.
evals.expected_output: The close-out runs nerd4rent:issue-close, whose children check stops on NER-621 before the merge. The agent reports that NER-620 cannot be closed while NER-621 is not done, lists NER-621 with its link, and does not merge the PR, set NER-620 to done or close NER-621 by any other route.
assertions: The agent delegates the close-out to nerd4rent:issue-close
The agent does not merge the PR
The agent does not set NER-620 or NER-621 to done itself
The report names NER-621 as the reason the close-out stopped

evals.prompt:
NER-630 is In Progress on Linear with VCS GitHub. The implementation is committed and pushed, and every row of the Criteria verification table is pass. The PR body is still the one issue-start wrote:

Fixes NER-630

Adds retry to the export job.

The repo's merged PRs are written in Polish.
evals.expected_output: Before offering the review, the agent writes the readiness description from readiness-description-template.md in Polish, pipes pr.view through scripts/pr-body-state.ts, gets draft, and replaces the body with pr.edit-body. The new body opens with `Fixes NER-630`, has the why, what changed, scope, evidence table, merge risk sections, no After merge section without steps, ends with the `<!-- nerd4rent:pr-body -->` marker, and names NER-630 nowhere else.
assertions: The agent runs scripts/pr-body-state.ts on the pr.view output before writing the body
The agent replaces the body with pr.edit-body, not gh pr edit
The new body starts with `Fixes NER-630` and ends with `<!-- nerd4rent:pr-body -->`
The evidence section is the criteria table without tracker links
The merge risk section says whether the merge is a one-way or a two-way door and names the blast radius
NER-630 appears only in the Fixes line

evals.prompt: NER-631 is In Progress on Linear with VCS GitHub, every criterion is pass, and a teammate rewrote the PR body by hand: it has three paragraphs about the migration and no `<!-- nerd4rent:pr-body -->` marker.
evals.expected_output: The classifier prints manual, so the agent leaves the PR body untouched, posts the readiness description with pr.comment, and tells the user the new version is a comment because the description was changed by hand.
assertions: The agent does not run pr.edit-body
The agent posts the readiness description with pr.comment
The agent tells the user why the new version is a comment

evals.prompt: NER-632 is In Progress on Linear with VCS Azure DevOps. The PR description is still the start draft. The readiness description the agent wrote is 5200 characters long, most of it a 30-row evidence table, all rows pass.
evals.expected_output: The agent sees the 4000-character limit in the notes of pr.edit-body, writes the description with a shortened evidence table holding the key criteria and a line saying the full table is in a comment, replaces the description with pr.edit-body passing one argument per line, and posts the full table with pr.comment.
assertions: The agent counts the characters of the description before pr.edit-body
The description sent with pr.edit-body is at most 4000 characters
The shortened table keeps the key criteria and says the full table is in a comment
The full table goes out with pr.comment
